summary: Hybrid batch job billed twice — embeddings and generation tokens both counted for same payload
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports a $18,340 spike on the March 1 invoice after a nightly hybrid batch job. The batch call included a mixed payload (generation + embeddings in one request) using the batch endpoint. Metering shows token counts duplicated across 'embedding_tokens' and 'generation_tokens' for the same request IDs. Customer believes they were billed twice for the same token usage.

Impact:
- Immediate financial impact: $18,340 unexpected invoice line. Customer is enterprise/dedicated and flagged for escalation.
- Reputational: customer is threatening to withhold renewal unless clarified.
- Operational: affects billing accuracy for mixed-payload customers during batch runs.

Timeline (as reported by customer):
- 2026-03-01 02:00 UTC: nightly batch job kicked off (scheduled internal job id batch-AZ-1029).
- 2026-03-01 02:03 - 02:20 UTC: batch completed (500k records).
- 2026-03-02: BrightCart reviewed invoice and noticed a +$18k delta compared to previous month.
- 2026-03-12: Customer opened support contact via portal.
- 2026-03-13: Initial triage by Support (ticket created).

Environment:
- Endpoint: /v1/batch (hybrid payload supported)
- Customer deploy mode: Dedicated (reserved pool) in us-east region
- Models invoked: embedder-v1 (embeddings), generation-v2 (text gen)

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Construct a hybrid batch payload where each record requests both an embedding and a short generation completion in the same request object.
2) Submit ~1000 record batch through /v1/batch using the batch client with streaming disabled.
3) Inspect metering records for request IDs; examine metric tags emitted by api-gateway and billing ingestion.
4) Observe duplicate attribution to embedding_tokens and generation_tokens for same token counts.

Customer-provided logs/attachments:
- customer-batch-log-2026-03-01.txt (request ids included)
- invoice_excerpt_Mar2026.pdf (line items highlighted)

Customer expectation:
- Immediate credit for the duplicated charge and a written explanation.

Workaround requested by customer:
- Manual invoice adjustment for March invoice and assurance this will not recur.
steps_to_reproduce: Prepare batch payload with both "embedding" and "generation" fields per record
Send payload to /v1/batch using the same API key and reserved pool in us-east
After completion, pull metering records via /internal/metering/events?request_id=<id>
Compare token counts emitted by api-gateway tags vs billing ingestion aggregation

2026-03-01T02:03:12Z billing-ingest INFO ingest_id=ing-988 request_id=abc123 metric=generation_tokens value=120
Invoice line: 2026-03-01 | Hybrid batch | 500k records | Amount: $18,340
investigation_notes: 03-13 Maya: initial triage — billing shows two metrics for same request ids; customer sample provided.
03-13 Leo: queried internal metering datastore; found duplicate events where router emitted both tags when hybrid payload present.
03-13 Eng hypothesis: recent router change (router v2.4.1) introduced metric tagging per subresponse instead of de-duping when payload requests multiple output types.
03-14 Billing: aggregation job sums embedding_tokens and generation_tokens independently; no de-dup logic for hybrid requests -> double charge.
Potential mitigations: invoice credit + hotfix to billing aggregation (de-dupe by request_id + token_offset) and router patch to emit unified token count for hybrid payloads.
Related: INT-889 flagged as a regression after router v2.4.1 rollout in us-east on 2026-02-28.

resolution: Workaround applied: Billing applied a provisional credit memo for the March invoice and will apply a final adjustment on the April invoice once root-cause is fixed. Engineering has a fix PR queued (github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4521) to add de-dup logic in the aggregation job and a router patch to normalize metrics for hybrid payloads. Postmortem and billing runbook update scheduled (Confluence page linked). Follow-up tasks: INT-889 rollback validation, QA of hybrid payload metering, and a customer-facing summary to be sent by Customer Success.
